title: Seating of the band and the rhythm section
summary: Braud explains how New Orleans bands sat together, with rhythm section close, and that guitar was used more than piano outside the district.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: I wanted to ask about the seating of the band. How did they sit or stand? In which order?
Well, just whatever order that the studio would place.
I mean, in the old New Orleans bands when you first heard them.
The old New Orleans band, we set all up in a bunch right together.
I mean, was the bass on one end or in the back?

The bass is on the rhythm sections always together. The drums and the piano are always together. You know, if it was possible. Sometimes it wasn't possible. But wherever it was possible, it was just the same, because we could feel each other. They used much piano then? Well, we were using piano the whole time I played. I never played as much with guitar the song around here. Yeah, well, I mean down here... We used to use guitar instead of piano around here, you know what I mean? Because you had more of one night stands. The only place that they used piano was in the district. Fellas like Buddy Christian, he was a great district man.
